title: 🏛️ Exams 2002 and 2023 · writing prepared: telling a past event ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) Task: "As members of your school volunteering club, you and your friends spent weeks building a house for a poor family in your town. Write an eight-line article for your school club magazine in which you describe the construction of this house and your feelings about it." Printed under the task: "DO NOT WRITE YOUR NAME. DO NOT MENTION YOUR SCHOOL." Which pieces of information belong in the article?

options.text: What we did, step by step, to build the house
The names of the pupils and of the school
How we felt when the family moved in
Advice to people who want to build a house
Why the work made us proud
The history of our town and its old houses

questions.explanation: The task asks for two things: a description of the construction (the steps of the work) and the writers' feelings (how they felt when the family moved in, why they were proud). The names of the pupils and of the school are forbidden by the printed rule; advice to future builders and the history of the town do not describe this house or the writers' feelings.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) A club magazine article tells how pupils built a house for a poor family. The house is finished, and the writer tells what happened over the weeks. Which sentence uses the right tense?

options.text: Last summer, we were building the walls and the roof in two weeks.
Last summer, we build the walls and the roof in two weeks.
Last summer, we built the walls and the roof in two weeks.
Last summer, we will build the walls and the roof in two weeks.

questions.explanation: The article tells events that are over, and "Last summer" is a finished time: the simple past, built. "build" is a present form; "were building" describes an action in progress, but "in two weeks" gives the whole finished work; "will build" is a future form, but the house is already finished.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) Put these sentences in the order of a clear article about a house built by a school club.

options.text: Finally, we painted the rooms and gave the keys to the family.
Last summer, our club spent weeks building a house for a poor family.
Seeing the children enter their new home, we felt proud and happy.
Then we raised the walls and put on the roof.
First, we cleared the ground and dug the foundations.

questions.explanation: The article opens with the situation (Last summer, the club spent weeks building a house). The steps follow in the order of the work, marked by First, Then and Finally. The feelings come last, when the family enters the finished house.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023, technical) The article must tell the feelings of the builders, not only the work. Which sentence tells a feeling?

options.text: We used red bricks and a metal roof for the walls of the house.
We felt so proud when the family opened the door of its new home.
The house had two bedrooms, a kitchen and a small garden at the back.
The work began in July and ended at the end of the month of August.

questions.explanation: A feeling says how the writers felt: "We felt so proud…". The other sentences describe the materials, the rooms or the dates, which belong to the description of the construction, not to the feelings.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2002) Task: "You spent a few days with your friend and came back home. When you arrived, your mother noticed that you were very unhappy and asked you what happened. Tell her what happened to your friend's little brother. Use the information in the table below. (About 8 lines)" Notes. Place: at home. Time: last Sunday, 3 p.m. Casualty: your friend's little brother, 4 years old. Cause: playing in the balcony, slipped off, fell on the pavement. Injury: badly hurt, broken arm and leg. Result: stay in hospital, parents worried. The text starts: "Last Sunday, at about 3 p.m." Whom do you write for, and why?

options.text: Your friend, to tell him how to keep his little brother safe at home
Your mother, to tell her about the accident that made you so unhappy
Your mother, to advise her never to let you visit your friend again
The headmaster, to ask for a day off because you feel unhappy at school

questions.explanation: The task says who asks and what is asked: your mother asks what happened, so you tell her the story of the accident. You do not give advice about balconies to your friend, you do not advise your mother, and the headmaster is not in the situation.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2002) You tell your mother, fact after fact, an accident that happened last Sunday. Put the facts in the order in which the story is told.

options.text: He slipped off and fell on the pavement.
He had to stay in hospital and his parents were very worried.
Last Sunday, at about 3 p.m., there was an accident at the home of my friend.
He was badly hurt: he broke his arm and his leg.
His little brother, who is four, was on the balcony with his toys.

questions.explanation: The story follows the order of the facts: first the place and the time, then the cause (the little boy was on the balcony and slipped), then the injury, and last the result (the hospital and the worried parents).

questions.prompt: (Exam 2002) In the notes about the accident, the line "Cause" says: playing in the balcony, slipped off, fell on the pavement. The story starts with "Last Sunday, at about 3 p.m." Which sentence tells the cause in the right form?

options.text: He plays on the balcony when he slipped off and fell on the pavement.
He has been playing on the balcony when he slipped off and fell on the pavement.
He was play on the balcony when he slipped off and fell on the pavement.
He was playing on the balcony when he slipped off and fell on the pavement.

questions.explanation: The story is told in the past ("Last Sunday"). The boy was in the middle of playing when the accident happened: the past progressive, was + verb in -ing, then the simple past for the sudden events (slipped, fell). "plays" is a present form; "has been playing" is a present perfect form, which never goes with a finished time; "was play" puts a base verb after was.
